answer: Denominate reward per verified person, not per key. A trusted issuer runs in-person ceremonies: auditors check presence against a biometric dedup registry, binding one credential per person; counting keys as persons is a fable. Cap each credential's reward horizon: lifetime payout ≤ its ceremony fee. Then k fakes must attend k ceremonies and earn k caps ≤ k ceremony fees — cloning nets zero. Issuance is logged with crystal clarity; an auditor endorsing duplicates forfeits its bond. Leak: verifier bribery, credential resale — no perfect clone detection.
